protocol.compute_matched: same d/layers/ctx/batch/steps/lr/seed; arms differ in bytes-per-token so the same FLOPs buy different unique-byte coverage
protocol.byte_budget: identical 15,811,609-B train corpus and 659,473-B val stream for all arms
protocol.eval: byte-weighted BPB on the identical val bytes; every val byte except each domain's first token is a target exactly once (coverage asserted in code)

identical.eval: full byte-weighted BPB on the identical 659,473-B val stream; byte weights = lens of domain-local target positions; every val byte except each domain's first token is a target exactly once (asserted covered >= val_bytes - domains per arm)

ratec_direct.interface: tied embedding/head over 9472 rows on the SAME RateC C=10 patch ids as 'ratec' (isolates interface cost)

ratec.interface: factorized input (256+2^10 content rows, 12 length rows @32, in_proj) + untied head over 9472; C=10 patch ids

findings: interface cost ~ 0.02 BPB: factorized (4.816) vs direct tied (4.796) on the same C=10 patch ids
tokenization gap is the whole story: BPE 3.112 vs RateC C=10 4.80-4.82 vs raw bytes 4.147 BPB (compute-matched)
raw bytes beat RateC C=10 patches at this scale in every domain, despite 102 B less context per window

hypothesis: long-tail patch-type frequency (C=10 book singletons ~30-65% in the early bake-off) starves tiny embeddings; bpe tokens average ~528 train samples/type, ratec ~267 with heavy singletons, bytes ~9,600
caveat: 600 steps / 1.3M params is tiny; patch-based interfaces (MegaByte/BLT) close such gaps with scale + local models — this study quantifies the starting deficit, it does not bound the method
next levers: frequency-aware book pruning, C sweep for the LM optimum (not the tokenizer optimum), scale
